# Introduction {.unnumbered}

Dataset source: <https://onlinestatbook.com/2/case_studies/binge.html>

::: {.content-visible when-profile="stata"}
{{< video https://youtu.be/qChry-CfQzM >}}

## Key concepts/commands:

1.  `use`: load in a dataset

    ```         
    use "https://learndata.net/binge.dta"
    ```

2.  `clear`: empty out any dataset so a new one can be loaded in

    ```         
    clear
    ```

3.  To make a simple comment in a do-file, use `//` or `*`

    ```         
    // This is a note to myself, called a "comment"
    * Here is another way to leave a note
    ```

4.  To make a multi-line (or partial-line) comment, use `/*` to start and `*/` to end

    ```         
    /*
    Here is a rather long comment.
    Maybe it is a note about how some of
    the variables were measured.
    */
    ```
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="r"}
## Model script

``` r
# This is a note to myself, called a "comment"
data <- read.csv("https://learndata.net/binge.csv")
View(data)
data$sex_text
data_posts <- read.csv("https://learndata.net/posts.csv")
```

## Key concepts/syntax:

1.  `read.csv()`: load in a dataset stored in "csv" format

    ``` r
    data <- read.csv("https://learndata.net/binge.csv")
    ```

2.  `View()`: show the data in a spreadsheet view

    ``` r
    View(data)
    ```

3.  referring to variables within a dataset: usually when you refer to a variable you also need to indicate the dataset, sometimes you can use `$` to connect the name of the dataset to the name of the variable (column)

    ``` r
    data$sex_text
    ```

4.  clear out workspace: in RStudio, click the broom icon in the "environment"

5.  To leave a comment in an R script, use `#`

    ``` r
    # This is a note to myself, called a "comment"
    ```

6.  Comment (or uncomment) several lines in a row: in RStudio, select the lines in the R script you want to modify, and then from the drop-down menu select Code \> Comment/Uncomment Lines
:::
